processing: Fully oxidised Ceylon black tea, sold in grades including OP and BOP1.
harvest_season: Year-round. One account says the tender leaf is picked after the first monsoon and processed in cooler weather.
appearance_dry: Dark leaf, longer and twisted in the OP grade, as is usual for that grade.
appearance_liquor: Coppery amber and clear, as is usual for lower-altitude Ceylon of this kind.
appearance_wet: Open coppery-brown leaf in the OP grade.
taste_profile: Described as creamy, with hints of cocoa, spice, tobacco and fruit: a rounder and softer cup than the brisk high-grown teas.

brewing.notes: Western style. A long OP leaf takes longer than broken grades, so give it four minutes or so.

vintage_note: Sold by estate and grade through the Colombo auction and on to merchants, without a vintage year. Ask for recent production and drink it within a year or two. BOP1 from this estate has reached record auction prices, so grade matters as much as the name.
description:
Kenilworth is a Ceylon estate near Ginigathena in Nuwara Eliya District, named after the castle in Warwickshire, and managed by Hatton Plantations PLC. It covers 603.11 hectares, with about 49% under tea.

The height is confusing, and it matters to how you think of this tea. Figures vary from around 640 m in the estate's more detailed accounts to 3,500 ft or more on merchants' pages, so don't treat it as a true high-grown tea on the strength of a shop label.

The usual description is creamy, with cocoa, spice, tobacco and fruit, and that fits a soft, round cup. Long-leaf OP is forgiving: four minutes, and milk is optional.

It is a familiar name on merchants' lists, usually as OP, and it has set auction records for BOP1. Check which grade you are buying, since the two brew very differently.
history:
Accounts place the estate's start around 1880, when British planters were moving from coffee to tea, with R.P. Rudd named as an early owner from 1880 to 1892. Another account says it was established at the turn of the last century, so the date is not fully settled.

It is listed today as the Kenilworth Group at Ginigathena, with Hatton Plantations PLC managing it and John Keells PLC acting as broker.
